summary: SMART-TC iteration 3 (Major Revision) — Backend: 15/16 tests pass for /dashboard/summary, /master-parts-search/lookup (q + cascading field), /spare-parts/{id}/stock-impact (no-IN branch), /stock/summary critical_list, /movements, /reports/movement-monthly, master-parts pagination (20/40/80/100). CRITICAL FAILURE: auto-IN helper `_try_auto_in` is defined at server.py line 906 but is NEVER CALLED from update_datang() — this breaks the entire stock IN/OUT lifecycle, stock-impact, and delete-reverse-OUT chain. Frontend: All UI checks pass — sidebar (7 items, no 'Data Sparepart'), Dashboard procurement+stock sections + Critical 'View All' modal, Master Data (pagination 20/40/80/100, 3 search fields, status filter options, NO Warning column, inline location edit, /database redirects to /area), /history renders, /parts/new autocomplete on Name returns master suggestions.

critical.issue: Auto-IN movement NEVER created. `_try_auto_in()` is defined at server.py:906 but is never invoked from `update_datang()` (or `_update_stage`). Consequences: (1) master_part.current_stock not incremented on Datang, (2) /spare-parts/{id}/stock-impact always returns has_in=False, (3) DELETE /spare-parts/{id} 'reverse OUT' branch can never execute since no IN exists. Verified by test_stock_impact_and_delete_reverse_flow — created master(stock=10) + matching spare-part(qty=3) + walked stages to DATANG; expected master.current_stock=13, got 10. Fix: in update_datang() (or end of _update_stage when stage=='DATANG' and merged.datang_date+datang_no set), call `await _try_auto_in(updated, user)`.

integration_issues.issue: UI 'Lanjutkan & Hapus' will work mechanically, but because backend never created the IN movement, the DeleteDialog's stock-impact call will always return has_in=false (no warning banner shown). Once backend auto-IN is wired, this flow will function end-to-end.

issues: Login redirects directly to /dashboard (not /area as stated in review request). This is actually a sensible default and matches the new sidebar — recommend updating the spec to /dashboard.

action_items: CRITICAL: Wire `_try_auto_in` into `update_datang` (or `_update_stage` post-update when stage=='DATANG' and datang_date+datang_no present). Without this, the entire IN/OUT history, stock-impact, and delete-reverse-OUT contract is broken.
Optional: update review-spec to note login redirects to /dashboard (matches new sidebar item order).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1391 lines — should be split into modules (auth, spare_parts, master_parts, movements, dashboard).

Master Data status filter is applied client-side AFTER backend pagination (line 1064-1065). This means when status filter is active, the returned page can have far fewer items than page_size, and `total` will overcount. Frontend pagination math will be off.
DELETE /spare-parts/{id} reverse-OUT logic itself is correct (creates adjustment movement, decrements master.current_stock, preserves IN history). Only blocked by missing auto-IN trigger.
GET /master-parts-search/lookup correctly uses ^q regex for prefix match on field-mode and contains-regex for q-mode — autocomplete UX is consistent.
/dashboard/summary loads up to 100000 parts/month and computes status in Python — fine at current scale but should move to MongoDB $facet aggregation if part count grows much past current 1000.
/stock/summary critical_list returns up to 200 items — adequate for popup; capped properly.

rca_of_the_critical_issue: Root cause: refactor introduced `_try_auto_in(part, user)` (server.py line 906) intended to be called when a Datang stage is recorded, but the call site was never added. `grep -n '_try_auto_in' server.py` returns only the definition line. Reproduction: 1) POST /master-parts {part_name,type,maker,line_area,stock_awal:10}. 2) POST /spare-parts with identical name/type/maker/line_area and qty_order=3. 3) PATCH /spare-parts/{id}/datang with datang_date+datang_no. 4) GET /master-parts/{mid} -> current_stock still 10 (expected 13). 5) GET /spare-parts/{id}/stock-impact -> {has_in:false}. Mitigation: at the end of `update_datang` (server.py line 728-731), after `_update_stage` returns, fetch the updated part and call `await _try_auto_in(updated_doc, user)`; or add to `_update_stage` a final `if stage=='DATANG' and merged.get('datang_date') and merged.get('datang_no'): await _try_auto_in(merged, user)`.
